correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed from a finite positive-mixture representation, strict Jensen convexity of \(u/(2-u)\), and monotone three-sample error conversion to \(4E^2+(3-2q+3q^2)E-q(1-q)^2\ge0\). The unique positive root is attained by one shifted inverse; differentiating it finds the maximizing spacing, and a positive-pole shifted argument gives the SPD witness. Boundary cases with no shifted inverses, a zero approximant, optional constant weight, endpoints in limiting spacing, all positive shifts, and arbitrary finite mixture lengths are handled. `check.py` passed 999 spacing checks and 2,000 random positive-mixture tests; only the written proof carries universal quantifiers.

A broader theorem explicitly describing the positive cone could dominate the claim, but none was available to inspect; the unavailable full text is a residual risk.

originality.rationale: Available material from the 2026 real-pole exponential paper and companion numerical implementations does not imply a sharp nonnegative-residue minimax error; inspected code uses an unconstrained coefficient solve. Older real-pole and unrestricted rational works were compared by statement and implications, not title alone. A targeted claims search did not locate the exact three-mode barrier, optimal spacing, uniquely attaining effective pole, or strictly SPD condition-9 witness. This is an evidence-limited scientific originality judgment, not exhaustive novelty certification.

value.rationale: The restriction to nonnegative positive-shift resolvent weights is motivated by genuinely parallelizable resolvent evaluations that preserve nonnegativity for inverse-positive matrix classes. Exact minimax algebra proves an >5% three-mode error floor regardless of the number of solves; the witness survives strict positive definiteness with spectral condition number 9 and ~3.9% floor. Sharp optimizing spacing and uniquely sufficient single pole clarify a structural design boundary rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
